# Godlights — Full API Reference

> Animated god ray / light beam effects for React.
> npm: `npm install godlights` | Docs: https://godlights.vercel.app/docs

---

## GodLights component

```tsx
import { GodLights } from "godlights";

<GodLights
  scene={scene}           // SceneConfig — required
  animate={false}         // boolean — enable RAF animation loop
  animParams={params}     // AnimParams — only used when animate=true
  showFps={false}         // boolean — dev FPS overlay (animate=true only)
  className="..."         // string — CSS class on wrapper div
  style={{ ... }}         // CSSProperties — inline style on wrapper div
/>
```

The wrapper div has `position: relative` by default. For full-bleed background:
```tsx
style={{ position: "absolute", inset: 0, width: "100%", height: "100%" }}
```
Do NOT rely on `className="absolute"` alone — inline style wins over Tailwind classes.

---

## SceneConfig

```ts
interface SceneConfig {
  width: number;      // canvas width in px (aspect ratio source; typically 1920)
  height: number;     // canvas height in px (typically 1080)
  noise: number;      // film grain intensity 0–100 (0 = none, 100 = heavy)
  grainSize: number;  // grain pixel size 1–4 (1 = fine, 4 = coarse)
  layers: Layer[];    // ordered back-to-front; layers[0] MUST be BackgroundLayer
}
```

**CRITICAL**: `layers[0]` must always be a `BackgroundLayer`. Without it the canvas is never cleared to a solid color, causing transparent frames and visual artifacts in animation.

---

## Layer types

### BackgroundLayer

```ts
interface BackgroundLayer {
  id: "background";        // must be the literal string "background"
  type: "background";
  bgType: "solid" | "gradient" | "transparent";
  bgColor: string;         // hex — primary / top color
  bgColor2: string;        // hex — secondary / bottom color (gradients)
  bgGradientAngle: number; // degrees: 0=up, 90=right, 180=down, 270=left
}
```

Example:
```ts
{
  id: "background",
  type: "background",
  bgType: "solid",
  bgColor: "#000000",
  bgColor2: "#000000",
  bgGradientAngle: 180,
}
```

### RayLayer

```ts
interface RayLayer {
  id: string;
  type: "rays";
  name: string;
  direction: number;          // angle rays point in degrees (0=up, 90=right, 180=down, 270=left)
  spread: number;             // angular width of the ray fan in degrees (0 = single beam, 180 = half-circle)
  originX: number;            // origin X as % of canvas width; can be <0 or >100 (off-screen sources)
  originY: number;            // origin Y as % of canvas height; can be <0 or >100
  rayCount: number;           // number of rays (1–200; 10–50 typical)
  rayWidth: number;           // ray width at origin (1–200)
  divergence: number;         // how much rays fan out along their length (0.1–5; 1 = natural, >2 = wide fan)
  rayLength: number;          // length as fraction of canvas diagonal (0.1–3; 0.5 = half diagonal)
  colorStart: string;         // hex color at ray origin
  colorEnd: string;           // hex color at ray tip
  opacity: number;            // overall layer opacity 0–1
  blendMode: BlendMode;       // see BlendMode section below
  fadeToTransparent: boolean; // fade tips to alpha=0 (true for soft rays)
  blur: number;               // gaussian blur in px 0–100 (10–30 typical)
  randomnessWidth: number;    // per-ray width variation 0–100
  randomnessLength: number;   // per-ray length variation 0–100
  randomnessAngle: number;    // per-ray angle variation 0–100 (0 = parallel rays, 100 = chaotic)
  seed: number;               // RNG seed — same seed = same random pattern every render
}
```

Example:
```ts
{
  id: "rays-1",
  name: "Main Rays",
  type: "rays",
  direction: 180,
  spread: 100,
  originX: 50,
  originY: -15,
  rayCount: 30,
  rayWidth: 80,
  divergence: 0.5,
  rayLength: 0.7,
  colorStart: "#3b82f6",
  colorEnd: "#06b6d4",
  opacity: 0.35,
  blendMode: "screen",
  fadeToTransparent: true,
  blur: 20,
  randomnessWidth: 80,
  randomnessLength: 30,
  randomnessAngle: 0,
  seed: 42,
}
```

### HaloLayer

```ts
interface HaloLayer {
  id: string;
  type: "halo";
  name: string;
  originX: number;       // center X as % of canvas width
  originY: number;       // center Y as % of canvas height
  color: string;         // hex color
  intensity: number;     // brightness 0–1 (0.2–0.6 typical)
  size: number;          // radius as fraction of canvas diagonal (0.01–2; 0.3–0.6 typical)
  blendMode: BlendMode;
}
```

Example:
```ts
{
  id: "halo-1",
  name: "Center Glow",
  type: "halo",
  originX: 50,
  originY: 0,
  color: "#3b82f6",
  intensity: 0.4,
  size: 0.6,
  blendMode: "lighter",
}
```

---

## BlendMode

```ts
type BlendMode =
  | "source-over"  // normal — no blending
  | "lighter"      // additive — bright, glowing (dark backgrounds only)
  | "screen"       // subtractive-inverse — soft glow (dark backgrounds only)
  | "overlay"      // contrast boost — works on mid-tone backgrounds
  | "soft-light"   // gentle contrast — works on most backgrounds
  | "hard-light";  // strong contrast
```

**Dark backgrounds** (`bgColor: "#000000"` or similar): use `"lighter"` or `"screen"`.
**Light backgrounds** (`bgColor: "#ffffff"` or similar): use `"multiply"` — NOTE: `"multiply"` is a valid canvas composite op but not in the BlendMode type. Use `"overlay"` or `"soft-light"` as alternatives, or swap to a dark background.

---

## AnimParams

```ts
interface AnimParams {
  speed: number;      // time multiplier — 0=frozen, 1=normal, 3=fast, 10=very fast
  angleAmp: number;   // ray angle oscillation 0–100 (0=no swing, 100=wild)
  lengthAmp: number;  // ray length oscillation 0–100
  widthAmp: number;   // ray width oscillation 0–100
  haloAmp: number;    // halo intensity oscillation 0–100
}
// NOTE: there is NO opacityAmp field. Adding it causes a TypeScript error.
```

Subtle animation:
```ts
{ speed: 1, angleAmp: 20, lengthAmp: 15, widthAmp: 10, haloAmp: 25 }
```

Dynamic animation:
```ts
{ speed: 3, angleAmp: 100, lengthAmp: 100, widthAmp: 100, haloAmp: 100 }
```

---

## Utility functions

```ts
// Draw one frame onto an existing canvas element
drawScene(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, scene: SceneConfig, time?: number, anim?: AnimParams, skipGrain?: boolean): void

// Export as PNG Blob (for download)
exportScene(scene: SceneConfig): Promise<Blob>

// Export as PNG data URL (for CSS background-image or <img src>)
exportDataURL(scene: SceneConfig): Promise<string>
```

Export example:
```ts
import { exportScene } from "godlights";

const blob = await exportScene(scene);
const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
const a = document.createElement("a");
a.href = url;
a.download = "rays.png";
a.click();
```

---

## Default values

```ts
import {
  DEFAULT_SCENE,           // complete scene with bg + halo + rays
  DEFAULT_RAY_LAYER,       // Omit<RayLayer, "id" | "name">
  DEFAULT_HALO_LAYER,      // Omit<HaloLayer, "id" | "name">
  DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_LAYER, // BackgroundLayer (black solid)
  DEFAULT_ANIM_PARAMS,     // { speed:1, angleAmp:50, lengthAmp:50, widthAmp:50, haloAmp:50 }
  BLEND_MODES,             // { value: BlendMode, label: string }[]
} from "godlights";

// Extend defaults to build a layer quickly
const myLayer: RayLayer = {
  ...DEFAULT_RAY_LAYER,
  id: "rays-1",
  name: "My Rays",
  colorStart: "#ff6600",
  colorEnd: "#ff6600",
};
```

---

## Full example — Next.js hero section

```tsx
"use client";

import { useMemo } from "react";
import { GodLights } from "godlights";
import type { SceneConfig } from "godlights";

const scene: SceneConfig = {
  width: 1920,
  height: 1080,
  noise: 10,
  grainSize: 1,
  layers: [
    // Always first — clears canvas to this color each frame
    {
      id: "background",
      type: "background",
      bgType: "solid",
      bgColor: "#000000",
      bgColor2: "#000000",
      bgGradientAngle: 180,
    },
    {
      id: "rays-1",
      name: "Main Rays",
      type: "rays",
      direction: 180,
      spread: 100,
      originX: 50,
      originY: -15,
      rayCount: 30,
      rayWidth: 80,
      divergence: 0.5,
      rayLength: 0.7,
      colorStart: "#3b82f6",
      colorEnd: "#06b6d4",
      opacity: 0.35,
      blendMode: "screen",
      fadeToTransparent: true,
      blur: 20,
      randomnessWidth: 80,
      randomnessLength: 30,
      randomnessAngle: 0,
      seed: 42,
    },
    {
      id: "halo-1",
      name: "Center Glow",
      type: "halo",
      originX: 50,
      originY: 0,
      color: "#3b82f6",
      intensity: 0.4,
      size: 0.6,
      blendMode: "lighter",
    },
  ],
};

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <section className="relative min-h-screen w-full overflow-hidden bg-black">
      <GodLights
        scene={scene}
        animate
        animParams={{
          speed: 1.2,
          angleAmp: 25,
          lengthAmp: 20,
          widthAmp: 15,
          haloAmp: 35,
          // ❌ opacityAmp does NOT exist — remove it
        }}
        style={{
          position: "absolute",
          inset: 0,
          width: "100%",
          height: "100%",
        }}
      />
      <div className="relative z-10 flex min-h-screen flex-col items-center justify-center">
        <h1 className="text-white">Your content here</h1>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

---

## Common mistakes checklist

1. ❌ **No BackgroundLayer** → canvas transparent each frame → add `{ id: "background", type: "background", ... }` as `layers[0]`
2. ❌ **`opacityAmp` in animParams** → TypeScript error → remove it, valid keys: `speed angleAmp lengthAmp widthAmp haloAmp`
3. ❌ **`className="absolute"` for positioning** → overridden by inline style → use `style={{ position: "absolute", inset: 0, ... }}`
4. ❌ **`blendMode: "screen"` on white background** → invisible rays → use `blendMode: "multiply"` on light backgrounds
5. ❌ **`blendMode: "multiply"` is not in `BlendMode` type** → TypeScript error → it IS a valid canvas op so cast: `blendMode: "multiply" as BlendMode`
